??? quote "Dialogue"

    - I am Prism! I paint pictures with lights, here at the gate, for whoever comes up the road. Did you see the cart? The little lit one, with people waving? That was the Walkers. I learned it from Nana Gristle. She says I got the basket wrong.
    - Lux promised! I still cannot believe it. I practise every night now. Fifty-three, last night, for nearly three breaths. Then I sat down very suddenly.
    - The frame is half woven! Every reed holds a light that does not tire. Two hundred, almost. Lux comes down from the towers to watch and does not say anything, which means it is good.
    - Ask me something! Or I will ask you something. I have so many.
        - *Choice:* What do you paint?
        - *Choice:* What is the Walkout Day show?
        - *Choice:* Where are you from?
        - *Choice:* Nothing. Goodbye.
    - The city's own stories! The Walkers' cart. The line of people with bundles. The first lanterns going up between the towers. Herons, because I like herons. I asked everyone in Urbanograd to tell me their stories. It has taken a year and I am not finished.
    - I only paint inside the walls, never toward the road. The Watch were worried lights in the dusk could be mistaken for other things. They were right to worry. Tick salutes my herons, though.
    - After the play, when the square is full, the whole Long Walk across the sky above Lantern Square, in light! Hundreds of lights. I have done forty. Once. I am a little frightened of standing in front of everybody and making three small sparks.
    - It is going to work. I think. The frame holds the lights, Lux dims the lanterns, and I only have to remember to breathe. On Walkout Day, stand in the middle of the square and look up!
    - Fairy Forest! My family weave baskets there. My gift is small: only little lights, a few breaths each. The Grove School taught me all the things it cannot do. No great workings, nothing a scholar would want.
    - But I wanted to make pictures with it, just because they are lovely, and I heard of a city where nobody needs a reason. So I walked out with the glass-carters two springs ago. The letters from home are mostly cheerful. Mostly.
    - Goodbye! Look up at the gate tonight. I will paint you something.
